lessons.title: Function Composition
learn: A function is a machine: input in, output out
g(f(x)) means f acts first, then g — read it inside out
Composition is not commutative: g(f(x)) ≠ f(g(x)) in general
Splitting a function into an inside and an outside part
lessons.try: If f(x) = x + 3 and g(x) = x², what is f(g(2))? Is it the same as g(f(2))?

lessons.title: Inverse Functions
learn: An inverse undoes a function, step by step in reverse order
To find it: swap x and y, then solve for y
The graph of an inverse is the mirror image across y = x
The horizontal line test, and restricting the domain
lessons.try: Find the inverse of f(x) = 3x − 5, and check that f⁻¹(f(2)) = 2.

lessons.title: Even & Odd Functions
learn: Even: f(−x) = f(x), a mirror image across the y-axis
Odd: f(−x) = −f(x), a half-turn around the origin
cos x is even and sin x is odd
The test: plug in −x and simplify
lessons.try: Is f(x) = x⁴ − 3x² even, odd, or neither? What about g(x) = x³ + 1?

lessons.title: Transformations of Functions
learn: f(x) + d shifts up; f(x − c) shifts right
a·f(x) stretches vertically, and a negative a flips over the x-axis
f(bx) squeezes horizontally, and a negative b flips over the y-axis
Outside changes act as expected; inside changes act backwards
lessons.try: Describe how y = −2√(x + 3) + 1 is built from y = √x, step by step.

lessons.title: Piecewise & Step Functions
learn: Each piece is drawn only over its own interval
Open circles vs closed dots at the endpoints
Jump discontinuities and one-sided behavior
Floor and ceiling functions make staircases
lessons.try: Parking costs $3 per hour or part of an hour. How much is 4 hours and 5 minutes?

lessons.title: Graphing Polynomials
learn: End behavior comes from the leading term
Zeros come from the factors
Single factor crosses, squared factor bounces, cubed factor flattens
Degree n allows at most n − 1 turning points
lessons.try: Sketch f(x) = x(x − 2)². Where does it cross, and where does it bounce?

lessons.title: Rational Functions & Asymptotes
learn: Vertical asymptotes where the denominator is zero
Behavior from the left and from the right of an asymptote
Horizontal asymptotes from comparing degrees
Holes (removable discontinuities) and slant asymptotes
lessons.try: Find all asymptotes and holes of f(x) = (x² − 4) / (x − 2)(x + 1).

lessons.title: Polynomial & Rational Inequalities
lessons.blurb: Sign charts on the number line.
learn: A polynomial can only change sign at a zero
Zeros split the number line into test intervals
Test one point in each interval and keep the ones you want
Rational inequalities never include the undefined points
lessons.try: Solve (x + 1)(x − 4) ≤ 0 and write the answer in interval notation.

lessons.title: Exponential Functions & e
learn: Linear growth adds; exponential growth multiplies
f(x) = a·bˣ: growth when b > 1, decay when 0 < b < 1
Half-life and decay models
Where e ≈ 2.718 comes from, and A = Peʳᵗ
lessons.try: $500 grows at 4% compounded continuously. How much is there after 5 years?

lessons.title: Logarithms
learn: log_b y = x means exactly the same as bˣ = y
The graph of a log is the mirror image of an exponential
Log rules are exponent rules in disguise
Using logs to solve exponential equations
lessons.try: Solve 3ˣ = 50. (Hint: take a log of both sides.)

lessons.title: Radians & Angular Velocity
learn: One radian is one radius of arc length
A full turn is 2π radians, so π rad = 180°
Arc length s = rθ
Linear speed v = rω
lessons.try: Convert 135° to radians. Then find the arc length it cuts on a circle of radius 4.

lessons.title: The Unit Circle, Unrolled
lessons.blurb: Where the sine wave really comes from.
learn: A radian is the distance travelled around a circle of radius 1
sin θ is the height of the point; cos θ is its horizontal position
Unrolling that height over time draws the sine wave
Why sine stays between −1 and 1 and repeats every 2π
lessons.try: What is sin(3π/2), and where is that point on the unit circle?

lessons.title: Special & Reference Angles
learn: The 45-45-90 triangle from half a square
The 30-60-90 triangle from half an equilateral triangle
Reference angles mirror the first quadrant
Signs by quadrant: All Students Take Calculus
lessons.try: Find cos(4π/3) using its reference angle and the quadrant sign.

lessons.title: Amplitude, Period & Phase Shift
lessons.blurb: Four dials that reshape any wave.
learn: A sets the amplitude, and a negative A flips the wave
B sets the period: 2π / B
C shifts the wave right — watch the minus sign
D moves the midline up or down
lessons.try: State the amplitude, period, phase shift and midline of y = 4 sin(3(x − π/6)) − 2.

lessons.title: Tangent & Reciprocal Graphs
lessons.blurb: When trig graphs go to infinity.
learn: tan θ is the slope of the radius on the unit circle
Tangent has period π and asymptotes where cos θ = 0
csc, sec and cot are 1/sin, 1/cos and 1/tan
Reciprocal graphs are big where the original is small
lessons.try: Where are the vertical asymptotes of y = sec x between 0 and 2π?

lessons.title: Inverse Trig Functions
learn: Sine fails the horizontal line test, so we restrict it
arcsin outputs angles from −π/2 to π/2
arccos outputs angles from 0 to π
Why sin⁻¹(1/2) = π/6, not 5π/6
lessons.try: Evaluate cos⁻¹(−√2/2). Which quadrant is the answer in?

lessons.title: Modeling with Sinusoids
lessons.blurb: A Ferris wheel becomes an equation.
learn: Read max, min, midline and amplitude from the situation
The period gives B = 2π / period
Choose sine or ±cosine from the starting point
Use the model to answer 'when' questions
lessons.try: A tide is highest (9 ft) at noon and lowest (1 ft) at 6 pm. Write a cosine model.

lessons.title: The Pythagorean Identity
lessons.blurb: sin² + cos² = 1 is just a triangle.
learn: The unit-circle triangle has legs cos θ and sin θ, hypotenuse 1
Pythagoras gives sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
Dividing gives tan²θ + 1 = sec²θ and 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ
Finding cos θ from sin θ and the quadrant
lessons.try: If cos θ = −5/13 and θ is in quadrant III, find sin θ.

lessons.title: Sum & Difference Identities
learn: A tilted triangle inside a rectangle proves the sum formulas
sin(α + β) = sin α cos β + cos α sin β
cos(α + β) = cos α cos β − sin α sin β
Differences: replace β with −β
lessons.try: Find the exact value of cos 15° using 45° − 30°.

lessons.title: Solving Trig Equations
lessons.blurb: Why there are infinitely many answers.
learn: Use the unit circle to find every angle in one turn
Add 2πk for the full family of solutions
Restrict to [0, 2π) when asked
Quadratic-style trig equations: substitute u = sin x
lessons.try: Solve 2cos x + 1 = 0 for 0 ≤ x < 2π.

lessons.title: The Law of Cosines
learn: c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C works for every triangle
When C = 90°, it becomes the Pythagorean theorem
Proof using coordinates and sin² + cos² = 1
Use it for SAS and SSS triangles
lessons.try: Two sides are 7 and 10 with a 120° angle between them. Find the third side.

lessons.title: Law of Sines & Bearings
lessons.blurb: Find the fire from two towers.
learn: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C
Proof by dropping a height
Bearings measure clockwise from north
Solving a two-tower location problem
lessons.try: In a triangle, A = 40°, B = 75° and a = 12. Find b.

lessons.title: Vectors
learn: Components ⟨x, y⟩ and magnitude by Pythagoras
Adding vectors tip to tail, and the parallelogram rule
Scalar multiplication stretches or flips a vector
A plane flying in a crosswind
lessons.try: Find the magnitude of ⟨−6, 8⟩ and the vector 3⟨2, −1⟩ + ⟨1, 4⟩.

lessons.title: Parametric Equations
learn: x and y both depend on time t
A projectile: where it lands and when
Eliminating t gives the regular equation
Orientation: the same circle traced two ways
lessons.try: Eliminate t from x = 2t + 1, y = t² to get y in terms of x.

lessons.title: Polar Coordinates
learn: (r, θ) means turn θ, then walk r
x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ
r = 2 is a circle; r = 2 sin 3θ is a rose
r = 1 + cos θ is a cardioid
lessons.try: Convert the point (−3, 3) to polar coordinates.

lessons.title: Conic Sections
learn: Circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola as slices of a double cone
Ellipse: the sum of distances to the foci is constant
Hyperbola: the difference of distances is constant
Finding the center, a, b and the foci from an equation
lessons.try: Find the center and foci of (x + 1)²/16 + (y − 2)²/7 = 1.

lessons.title: Arithmetic Sequences & Series
learn: Recursive vs explicit formulas: aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d
Gauss's trick: pair the first and last terms
Sₙ = n(a₁ + aₙ) / 2
Counting seats in a theater
lessons.try: Find the sum 5 + 9 + 13 + … + 101.

lessons.title: Infinite Geometric Series
learn: ½ + ¼ + ⅛ + … fills a square exactly
Partial sums: Sₙ = a(1 − rⁿ) / (1 − r)
The infinite sum is a / (1 − r), but only if |r| < 1
The bouncing ball problem
lessons.try: Find the sum 12 + 4 + 4/3 + 4/9 + …

lessons.title: Sigma Notation
learn: Reading Σ: where to start, where to stop, what to add
Expanding and evaluating a sum
Writing arithmetic and geometric series in sigma form
Pulling out constants and splitting sums
lessons.try: Evaluate the sum from k = 1 to 4 of (3k − 2).

lessons.title: The Binomial Theorem
learn: (a + b)² as areas in a square
Coefficients count which brackets give you b
Pascal's triangle
(a + b)ⁿ = Σ C(n, k) aⁿ⁻ᵏ bᵏ
lessons.try: Find the coefficient of x³ in (x + 3)⁵.
